lines: Emulation of the Spin Semiconductor FV-1 reverb and effects chip, running an assembler program loaded from a .spn file, with the chip's three control pots brought out as knobs
Sets the loaded program’s first control, 0 to 1; what it changes is decided by the program, and the display names it when the program comes from a bank that says
Sets the loaded program’s second control, 0 to 1; what it changes is decided by the program, and the display names it when the program comes from a bank that says
Sets the loaded program’s third control, 0 to 1; what it changes is decided by the program, and the display names it when the program comes from a bank that says
Attenuverter on the CV jack for the first control, and at its centre when the module is added, which leaves that jack doing nothing
Attenuverter on the CV jack for the second control, and at its centre when the module is added, which leaves that jack doing nothing
Attenuverter on the CV jack for the third control, and at its centre when the module is added, which leaves that jack doing nothing
Balances untreated signal against the program’s output: anticlockwise gives the untreated signal alone and stops the emulator, clockwise gives the program alone, the centre gives both at full level
Attenuverter on the DRY/WET jack, and at its centre when the module is added, which leaves that jack doing nothing
Trims the left input going into the emulator: silent fully anticlockwise, unchanged at the centre, and doubled fully clockwise
Trims the right input going into the emulator: silent fully anticlockwise, unchanged at the centre, and doubled fully clockwise
Steps back one program in the loaded FX bank, or back through the .spn files in the folder the current program came from when no bank is loaded
Steps on one program in the loaded FX bank, or on through the .spn files in the folder the current program came from when no bank is loaded
Adds to the first control, a tenth of a unit per volt with its attenuverter fully open, on the knob's own 0 to 1 scale
Adds to the second control, a tenth of a unit per volt with its attenuverter fully open, on the knob's own 0 to 1 scale
Adds to the third control, a tenth of a unit per volt with its attenuverter fully open, on the knob's own 0 to 1 scale
Adds to the dry and wet balance, half a unit per volt with its attenuverter fully open, on the knob's own -1 to +1 scale
The left input; with nothing patched into the right input the right channel is fed silence rather than this signal
The right input; with nothing patched into the left input the left channel is fed silence rather than this signal
The left channel, the trimmed left input and the program's left output mixed by DRY/WET, clipped to ±10V
The right channel, the trimmed right input and the program's right output mixed by DRY/WET, clipped to ±10V
Menu — Select SPN File... — opens a file chooser for one FV-1 assembler program, and the arrow buttons then step through the other .spn files in that same folder
Menu — Parser log... — writes what the assembler made of the loaded program into a file beside the plugin and opens it
Menu — Select FX-Bank... — on the display's own menu rather than the panel's: opens a file chooser for a programs.json holding many programs at once
Note — Clicking the display with either mouse button opens its own menu, which is where the FX bank is loaded and where the bank's programs are listed by category.
Note — The module comes up with demo.spn, the one program shipped with the plugin, so the arrow buttons do nothing until another .spn file or an FX bank is loaded.
Note — A bank of 157 programs is published as programs.json in the maker's repository; it is not part of the plugin and has to be fetched and loaded.
Note — All four attenuverters are at their centre when the module is added, so none of the four CV jacks does anything until one is turned.
Note — Each jack carries one channel, so a polyphonic cable is reduced to its first channel.
Note — The back arrow cannot reach the first program of a bank: stepping back from the second jumps to the last instead.

FV-1emu.notes: No parameter, input or output is given a name: every configParam call passes an empty string and there are no configInput or configOutput calls at all, so Rack's tooltips are blank on the whole panel. The DRY/WET law is not a crossfade: d = clamp(1 - mix, 0, 1) and w = clamp(1 + mix, 0, 1) with mix running -1 to +1, so the centre position passes the untreated signal and the program's output both at full level, summed. When w reaches 0 the emulator is not run at all that sample. The three control CV jacks are scaled by 0.1 before their attenuverters while the DRY/WET jack is not scaled at all, so a volt reaches two and a half times further there in proportion to its knob's travel. The input trims multiply by (1 + value) over a -1 to +1 parameter, so the anticlockwise end silences that input. The back-arrow branch reads `if (--selectedProgram <= 0) selectedProgram = programs.size() - 1`, which skips index 0. The plugin ships only fx/demo.spn and fx/README.TXT; there is no programs.json in the installed folder. The display's draw() uses Rack's deprecated NVGcontext* signature, which still works.
